create.title: Actual distinct-radical termwise absolute Fourier certificate obstruction
create.statement_tex: Fix a nonnegative real radial smooth unit-mass mollifier supported in the unit disk, Psi(s)=rho-hat(s e1), a nonnegative smooth w supported in [1/2,2] with positive integral, fixed even p=2k>=4 and fixed 0<=alpha<1. For real T sufficiently large set Q=floor(T^alpha), a_n=r2(n)n^(-3/4)Psi(sqrt(n/T)). Choose fixed c>0 small enough that Psi>=1/2 on sqrt(c)<=s<=sqrt(2c), and retain integers N_T={cT<=n<=2cT:sf(n)>Q}. Then T 2^(-p) sum_(ordered n_1,...,n_p in N_T; sf(n_i) pairwise distinct) product_i a_(n_i) |w-hat(-T[sum_(i<=k)sqrt(n_i)-sum_(i>k)sqrt(n_i)])| >=c_(p,alpha,rho,w) T^(p/4-1/2). This is a positive subcollection of the complete termwise absolute distinct-class Fourier expansion. Its proof retains actual coefficients, all harmonics in the selected block, all repeated-class exclusion, ordered multiplicities and real endpoints. Distinct squarefree classes make each retained frequency nonzero. At p=12,alpha=2/5 the lower bound T^(5/2) rules out closing the29/25 target by this termwise absolute certificate. It is not a lower bound for signed I_p or any physical moment, does not reject the signed target or quarter theorem, and is not uniform for p growing with T.
